---
output: word_document
knit: (function(inputFile, encoding) {
    rmarkdown::render(
      inputFile,
      encoding = encoding,
      output_dir = here::here("paper")
    )
  })
---
  
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(pdftools)
library(knitr)
```

```{r convert-and-insert, results='asis'}
# 1. Locate all single-page PDFs (adjust path or pattern as needed)
pdf_files <- list.files(path = here::here("doc", "gear_diagrams"), pattern = "\\.pdf$", full.names = TRUE)

# Sort files if order matters (e.g., numerically or alphabetically)
pdf_files <- sort(pdf_files)

# 2. Define an output directory for converted images
temp_img_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "pdf_images")
dir.create(temp_img_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# 3. OpenXML snippet for inserting page breaks into Word (.docx)
page_break <- "\n\n```{=openxml}\n<w:p><w:r><w:br w:type=\"page\"/></w:r></w:p>\n```\n\n"

# 4. Loop through each PDF, convert to PNG, and output markdown
for (i in seq_along(pdf_files)) {
  pdf_path <- pdf_files[i]
  
  img_path <- pdf_convert(
    pdf = pdf_path,
    pages = 1,
    format = "png",
    dpi = 300,
    filenames = file.path(temp_img_dir, paste0("page_", i, ".png")),
    verbose = FALSE
  )
  
  cat(sprintf("![](%s)\n", normalizePath(img_path, winslash = "/")))
  
  # # Insert a page break after each page except the last
  # if (i < length(pdf_files)) {
  #   cat(page_break)
  # }
}
```
